packet.headline_seed: 'If we die, we die together': Wife of man nearly sucked out of Ryanair plane speaks of ordeal
packet.description_seed: Svetlana Grković told Serbian media that her husband is "seriously injured and in shock".

what: 'If we die, we die together': Wife of man nearly sucked out of Ryanair plane speaks of ordeal

clean_source_blocks.text: The pair were returning from holiday in Thessaloniki, Serbian media reports A woman who held the legs of her husband as he was nearly sucked head-first out of a Ryanair cabin window on Friday said "half of his body was sticking out of the plane." Svetlana Grković, who was travelling with her husband Ljubisa Karović from Greece's Thessaloniki to Germany's Memmingen, told Greek public broadcaster ERT he was "outside up to his chest" for two minutes. "I immediately reacted and grabbed his legs. I thought: 'If we die, we die together,'" Grković told Serbian outlet Nova. With the help of two other passengers, Grković said she was able to pull her husband - who she said lost consciousness three times - back inside.

A woman has described the terrifying mid-air battle to stop her husband being completely sucked out of an aircraft window after it shattered. Serbian couple Ljubiša Karović and Svetlana Grković were on board a Ryanair flight travelling from Greece to Germany when debris from an engine failure struck and broke a window next to them last Friday, the Daily Mail reported. The window completely blew out and Karović was partially dragged out of the cabin. His wife gripped his legs as he hung outside the aircraft, the Greek outlet Protothema reported. The aircraft was forced to abandon its journey and return to Thessaloniki for an emergency landing after reaching nearly 5000m. Passengers reported hearing a loud explosion shortly after take-off before discovering the damage, the Daily Mail reported.
Svetlana Grković told Serbian media that her husband is "seriously injured and in shock".

Serbian couple Ljubiša Karović and Svetlana Grković were on board a Ryanair flight when a window next to them blew out. Photo / Ljubiša Karović and Svetlana Grković Speaking afterwards, Grković described the incident, which occurred as the couple were returning home from a holiday in Greece. “It was as if a part of the engine broke off and hit the window next to which my husband Ljubiša was sitting,” she told Serbian broadcaster Nova. “I reacted immediately and grabbed his legs. I thought: ‘If we die, we die together.’ It was horrible.” In the chaos, some passengers rushed to help the couple. Grković said two people helped almost immediately, helping her stop her husband being dragged from the plane.

payload.title: Mies tempautui osittain ulos Ryanairin koneen ikkunasta – vaimo piti kiinni jaloista
payload.summary: Svetlana Grković ja kaksi muuta matkustajaa vetivät Ljubiša Karovićin takaisin matkustamoon rikkoutuneen ikkunan luota. Kone palasi Thessalonikiin hätälaskua varten.
payload.content:
Serbialainen Svetlana Grković kertoo pitäneensä kiinni miehensä Ljubiša Karovićin jaloista, kun tämä tempautui pää edellä osittain ulos rikkoutuneesta matkustamon ikkunasta Ryanairin lennolla perjantaina. Kreikan Thessalonikista Saksan Memmingeniin matkalla ollut kone keskeytti lennon ja palasi Thessalonikiin hätälaskua varten. Grkovićin mukaan miehen kehosta noin puolet oli pahimmillaan koneen ulkopuolella.

Vaimo ja matkustajat vetivät miehen sisään

Karović istui ikkunan vieressä, kun se hajosi. Grković kertoi Kreikan yleisradioyhtiö ERT:lle, että hänen miehensä oli rintaansa myöten koneen ulkopuolella noin kahden minuutin ajan. Hänen kuvauksensa mukaan Karovićin ylävartalo oli avoimen ikkunan ulkopuolella, kun hän itse piti miehensä jaloista kiinni matkustamon sisällä. Karović menetti tilanteen aikana tajuntansa kolmesti.

Grković sanoi reagoineensa välittömästi ikkunan rikkouduttua. ”Ajattelin: jos kuolemme, kuolemme yhdessä”, hän kertoi serbialaiselle Nova-medialle. Vaimon mukaan kaksi muuta matkustajaa saapui lähes heti auttamaan. Kolmikko onnistui pitämään Karovićin koneessa ja vetämään hänet lopulta takaisin matkustamoon. Grković kuvasi kokemusta hirvittäväksi.

Voimakas ääni edelsi ikkunan rikkoutumista

Tilanne alkoi pian lentoonlähdön jälkeen, jolloin matkustajat kertoivat kuulleensa voimakkaan räjähdyksen. Grkovićin mukaan vaikutti siltä, että moottorista irronnut osa osui hänen miehensä vieressä olleeseen ikkunaan. Ikkuna rikkoutui kokonaan, ja Karović tempautui pää edellä osittain ulos koneesta. Tapahtuma aiheutti matkustamossa nopeasti kaoottisen tilanteen.

Lento oli matkalla Thessalonikista Memmingeniin, ja pariskunta oli palaamassa Kreikassa vietetyltä lomalta. Kone oli ehtinyt nousta lähes 5 000 metrin korkeuteen, mutta matka Saksaan keskeytettiin ja kone käännettiin takaisin Thessalonikiin. Siellä se teki hätälaskun.

Tapahtumien kulku perustuu pääosin Grkovićin kertomukseen. Hän kuvasi kokemusta sekä Kreikan yleisradioyhtiö ERT:lle että serbialaiselle Nova-medialle ja luonnehti tilannetta hirvittäväksi. Grković kertoi myöhemmin Serbian medialle miehensä olevan vakavasti loukkaantunut ja sokissa. Tarkempia tietoja Karovićin vammojen laadusta tai hänen voinnistaan tapahtuman jälkeen ei julkaistuissa tiedoissa kerrottu.
summary_bullets: Ljubiša Karović tempautui osittain ulos rikkoutuneesta matkustamon ikkunasta.
Svetlana Grković ja kaksi muuta matkustajaa vetivät hänet takaisin koneen sisälle.
Lento keskeytettiin ja kone palasi Thessalonikiin hätälaskua varten.
payload.journalist_note: Tapahtumankulku on kirjoitettu silminnäkijäkertomuksina. Moottorinosan mahdollinen osuma esitetään Grkovićin arviona, ei varmistettuna teknisenä syynä.

Tapahtumien kulku perustuu pääosin Grkovićin kertomukseen. Hän kuvasi kokemusta sekä Kreikan yleisradioyhtiö ERT:lle että serbialaiselle Nova-medialle ja luonnehti tilannetta hirvittäväksi. Grković kertoi myöhemmin Serbian medialle miehensä olevan vakavasti loukkaantunut ja sokissa. Tarkempia tietoja Karovićin vammojen laadusta tai hänen voinnistaan tapahtuman jälkeen ei julkaistuissa tiedoissa kerrottu.

The pair were returning from holiday in Thessaloniki, Serbian media reports A woman who held the legs of her husband as he was nearly sucked head-first out of a Ryanair cabin window on Friday said "half of his body was sticking out of the plane." Svetlana Grković, who was travelling with her husband Ljubisa Karović from Greece's Thessaloniki to Germany's Memmingen, told Greek public broadcaster ERT he was "outside up to his chest" for two minutes. "I immediately reacted and grabbed his legs. I thought: 'If we die, we die together,'" Grković told Serbian outlet Nova. With the help of two other passengers, Grković said she was able to pull her husband - who she said lost consciousness three times - back inside.

A woman has described the terrifying mid-air battle to stop her husband being completely sucked out of an aircraft window after it shattered. Serbian couple Ljubiša Karović and Svetlana Grković were on board a Ryanair flight travelling from Greece to Germany when debris from an engine failure struck and broke a window next to them last Friday, the Daily Mail reported. The window completely blew out and Karović was partially dragged out of the cabin. His wife gripped his legs as he hung outside the aircraft, the Greek outlet Protothema reported. The aircraft was forced to abandon its journey and return to Thessaloniki for an emergency landing after reaching nearly 5000m. Passengers reported hearing a loud explosion shortly after take-off before discovering the damage, the Daily Mail reported.

Svetlana Grković told Serbian media that her husband is "seriously injured and in shock".

Serbian couple Ljubiša Karović and Svetlana Grković were on board a Ryanair flight when a window next to them blew out. Photo / Ljubiša Karović and Svetlana Grković Speaking afterwards, Grković described the incident, which occurred as the couple were returning home from a holiday in Greece. “It was as if a part of the engine broke off and hit the window next to which my husband Ljubiša was sitting,” she told Serbian broadcaster Nova. “I reacted immediately and grabbed his legs. I thought: ‘If we die, we die together.’ It was horrible.” In the chaos, some passengers rushed to help the couple. Grković said two people helped almost immediately, helping her stop her husband being dragged from the plane.
